Seven review dimensions covered: correctness—an in-flight read can issue a stale ownership claim after pause, and recovery can reject or lose its original target; conventions—the inspected changes otherwise retain memory-only runtime state, configuration-only persistence, stable identities, explicit errors and separate PTY processing; behavior tests—the added tests exercise real CLI/controlling-PTY behavior, effects and cleanup, but do not cover pause between claim RPCs, recovery during bootstrap, cleared profile defaults or observation loss after an acknowledged launch; design—the existing broker and original-connection worker are reused without dependencies or a generic plugin layer, but launch/recovery state publication is not failure-atomic; edge cases—A02–A04 identify concrete startup, clearing and lost-reply failures; security—A01 permits stale authority acquisition/reservation across the new pause fence, while no additional supported injection, credential-disclosure or permission-responder defect was established; Fowler smells—Duplicated Code is evident in the inconsistent null-to-first-session identity rules behind A02, with no separate speculative smell findings added.
This was read-only source review of the frozen E06 scope and its requirements/threat model: I made no edits and executed no builds, tests, lint, formatting, programs, provider/auth calls or private-fixture reads; the parent's reported passing regressions and native smoke are evidence supplied by the parent, not checks executed by me, and full live acceptance remains separately failing after eight of nine approved requests because the private guard blocked final continuation, which is not itself counted as a production-source defect or waived by this review, with physical suspend, Linux and minimum-toolchain execution still unproven.
